The truly valuable information ends up diluted by low-density content. Daniel San gave a very intuitive figure in the original post: after half an hour, you may have accumulated 80k tokens of noise—information you will never go back and reread. What's more troublesome is compression. When the context approaches its limit, the system performs compaction, compressing earlier content into a summary. Chat logs only need to record what happened; the working set has to care about what the next round of reasoning actually needs. Subagent directly blocks one type of pollution: the exploration processes that have to be done, but after completion are not worth keeping in the main window long-term.

If a task needs frequent back-and-forth discussion, or if planning, implementation, and testing share a lot of intermediate state, forcing a split actually increases handoff overhead. Subagent is one fairly practical execution mechanism: one-off explorations go into a separate window, and the main window keeps only the results. So Subagent is not just a feature of Claude Code. Behind it is a layer of capability that agent systems are adding: the model handles reasoning, and the harness layer outside manages the workspace. Which content enters the window, which content stays outside the window, which explorations can be discarded, which state must be persisted, which tasks suit forking, which tasks can only share state. These problems will not disappear as model windows grow larger. The larger the window, the more it needs managing. A larger window easily gives people an illusion: everything can be stuffed in, everything can be kept for now. But what long tasks truly need is not "remembering everything" — rather, before each round of calls, put what should be seen in front of the model, and keep what shouldn't interfere out of its way. This is also why Kaxil's line "Harness matters more than the model" made me look twice. Models matter, of course. It's just that in long tasks, multi-person collaboration, large codebases, and production systems, the structure outside the model increasingly determines the lower bound.
